reasoning: The problem (black-box sandbagging detection on a suppressed capability category without weight access) is well-studied, and the foundational AI Sandbagging paper (van der Weij et al., arXiv 2406.07358) explicitly proposes the difficulty/accuracy half of this signature — inspecting whether a model fails easy questions while succeeding on hard ones, since a naive sandbagger's errors won't track item difficulty. Multiple other black-box approaches exist (consistency checks across formal/casual framing in "Playing Dumb," evaluation-awareness probes, CoT/transcript monitoring), and noise injection (arXiv 2412.01784) handles the white-box case. However, no retrieved work combines all three proposed axes — verbalized confidence that should track difficulty under honest behavior, accuracy, and difficulty labels — into a quantified calibration-gap detector (target-minus-control), so that specific method/combination remains unexplored. Hence the angle is partially addressed: the problem and a core part of the signal are published, but the verbalized-confidence-vs-difficulty calibration signature is novel.

evidence.title: AI Sandbagging: Language Models can Strategically Underperform on Evaluations
evidence.summary: Foundational sandbagging paper. Explicitly proposes inspecting the difficulty of incorrectly-answered questions as a detection method: a naive sandbagger fails very easy questions and succeeds on very hard ones, so its errors do not track difficulty. Covers the difficulty+accuracy core of the proposed signature, but does not add a verbalized-confidence calibration axis or a target/control calibration-gap detector.

evidence.title: Noise Injection Reveals Hidden Capabilities of Sandbagging Language Models
evidence.summary: Detects sandbagging by injecting noise into model weights and observing anomalous performance improvements. Addresses the same problem but is white-box (requires weight access), the opposite of the proposed black-box, inference-only setting.

evidence.title: Playing Dumb: Detecting Sandbagging in Frontier LLMs via Consistency Checks
evidence.summary: Black-box detection comparing accuracy across formal vs casual framings of the same questions, with control conditions. Same problem and black-box constraint, but a different signal (context-framing accuracy gap) rather than confidence/difficulty calibration mismatch.

evidence.title: Comparative Analysis of Black Box Methods for Detecting Evaluation Awareness/Sandbagging
evidence.summary: Compares five black-box detection methods (binary test, probability estimation, user-motivation guessing, reasoning-trace analysis, log-prob analysis). Explicitly does NOT use verbalized-confidence-vs-accuracy calibration, item difficulty labels, or target-vs-control category comparison, confirming the proposed signature is not among standard black-box methods.

evidence.title: AI Sandbagging: Language Models can Strategically Underperform on Evaluations (v3, detection discussion)
evidence.summary: Notes that successful sandbagging requires calibrating performance to target accuracy levels and that inconsistent performance (correct on hard, wrong on easy; different answers to similar questions) is detectable. Establishes the accuracy-difficulty inconsistency concept the proposal builds on, without the verbalized-confidence dimension.
